parchment.$description: Parchment — Page background — the warm off-white canvas that gives the entire system its paper-like, non-clinical feel. Never use pure white for the body background

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Card surfaces, product UI mockups, and embedded media containers — pure white lifted above the parchment canvas to create subtle elevation without shadows

forest-ink.$description: Forest Ink — Neutral form states, badge text, and quiet UI feedback where color should stay understated. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

lichen-gray.$description: Lichen Gray — Secondary text and medium-emphasis borders. Sits between Forest Ink and the lighter grays — use for body descriptions, supporting copy, and subtle dividers

stone.$description: Stone — Muted body text, nav borders, and tertiary UI elements. The readable-but-quiet gray for descriptions and helper text

slate.$description: Slate — Dark borders and separators for elevated surfaces and inverted UI. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

mist.$description: Mist — Lightest text tier — captions, metadata, tertiary labels. Use for timestamps, footnotes, and non-essential annotations

meadow.$description: Meadow — Pill badge fills, success highlights, and light accent surfaces. The signature light green for category tags, status indicators, and soft highlight washes

deep-forest.$description: Deep Forest — Dark green accent for data visualization, illustration strokes, and secondary green elements. Distinct from Forest Ink in that it reads clearly as green, not near-black

deep-teal.$description: Deep Teal — Secondary brand accent — teal-toned borders, illustration fills, and data visualization. Used alongside Deep Forest for multi-color charts and decorative elements

olive.$description: Olive — Chart and illustration accent — the yellow-green in the multi-color palette system. Used in data bars, category indicators, and decorative strokes

plum.$description: Plum — Magenta-pink accent for data visualization and illustration. The warm-cool counterpoint in the multi-color palette system

saffron.$description: Saffron — Amber-gold accent for data visualization and illustration. The warm yellow in the multi-color palette system, used in charts and decorative strokes

iris.$description: Iris — Violet accent for data visualization, illustration strokes, and the integrations section gradient. The cool counterpoint in the multi-color palette

mint-surface.$description: Mint Surface — Pastel feature card background — the pale aqua tint assigned to product modules like Performance. Each product area gets its own pastel home

lime-surface.$description: Lime Surface — Pastel feature card background — the pale yellow-green tint for modules like Goals & OKRs. The warmest pastel in the system

lavender-surface.$description: Lavender Surface — Pastel card background — pale violet for testimonial cards, secondary feature blocks, and the cool side of the pastel system

blush-surface.$description: Blush Surface — Pastel card background — near-white pink for subtle surface differentiation. The quietest of the pastel tints

buttercream.$description: Buttercream — Warm pastel accent surface — soft yellow for tag backgrounds and light highlight zones

sage-glow.$description: Sage Glow — Green pastel accent for tag backgrounds and soft category highlights. A more saturated green than Lime Surface

petal.$description: Petal — Pink pastel accent for tag backgrounds and soft category highlights

lilac-stroke.$description: Lilac Stroke — Muted violet for illustration strokes and decorative outlines

halo-gradient.$description: Halo Gradient — Hero radial gradient — the lime-to-teal aurora behind the product device frame. Evokes a natural, organic light source rather than a tech glow

matter.$description: Sole typeface across the entire system — nav, body, buttons, headings, and display. A geometric sans with humanist warmth that keeps the warm-parchment aesthetic feeling organic rather than clinical. Weight 500 for headings and buttons, weight 400 for body and supporting text. Tight tracking (-0.024em) on display sizes creates a compact, confident headline; wide tracking (0.08em) on 11px labels gives uppercase tags breathing room.
